frozen: 2026-11-01, after addenda salmon2-5 (their results by area and group are known: with upstream thinning the Northwest Coast and California gain strongly, but Arctic and Hudson Bay groups on rivers to ice-covered seas become far too dense: Utkuhikhalingmiut, Caribou Inuit, Aivilingmiut, Attawapiskat and Rupert House Cree). Because the Northwest Coast and the interior have now been seen several times, no area is blind any more; the decision uses leave-one-culture-area-out cross-validation instead.
change: the salmon index of addendum salmon4 (HydroRIVERS streams >= 1 m3/s, not endorheic, <= 1,500 km from the outlet, weighted by exp(-distance to the outlet / L)) counting only systems whose outlet's WOA18 annual-mean sea surface is between 2 and 15 C in the Northern Hemisphere: seas below 2 C are ice-covered most of the year (the Arctic Ocean, Hudson Bay), where salmon runs are small or absent, while the Bering Sea's salmon rivers (the Yukon, the Kuskokwim) reach 3-5 C
model: configuration D (600-year mean; a_marine 3000, a_fresh 100, k_terr 0.5) + a_salmon x S_salmon(L); a_salmon in {0, 30, 100, 300, 1000}, L in {100, 200, 400, 800} km
cross_validation: folds = the culture areas ARC, NNA, WNA, BC NWC, SW, and the rest of the world as one fold; for each fold, (a_salmon, L) minimising the median absolute log10 error over the other folds' groups predicts the held-out fold; the CV error is the median absolute log10 error of all held-out predictions. The baseline is configuration D (a_salmon 0).
adopt_if: the CV error improves on the baseline by at least 0.02, no fold's held-out median absolute log10 error worsens by more than 0.05, and the rest-of-world fold's is not worse by more than 0.01. Then (a_salmon, L) are fitted on all groups and data/foraging_model.json takes them (the map: drawn rivers reaching a sea between 2 and 15 C annual, weighted by distance along them to the sea, scaled to HydroRIVERS' stream density), and the atlases' foraging is rebuilt.
